title: sprint-reset-1on1-scratch-harper-gomes-jun12-2028
body:
Purpose: quick sync to recalibrate priorities after last sprint spike and unblock the latency regression work. Short (~30 min).

Agenda (30m):
- 5m: Quick status: health of current workstreams (where we sit vs sprint commitment)
- 8m: Latency regression deep-dive — current hypothesis, evidence, next experiments
- 6m: Career/check-in — confidence, workload, ramps, promotion readiness signals
- 6m: Blockers & support needs (infra, cross-team, hiring)
- 5m: Agree actions and owners; calendar follow-ups

Notes to self (pre-meeting):
- Brevity: bring 1 slide equivalent in words. Start with the one-line ask at top.
- Ask: decision on whether to pause feature X rollout until regression removed, or continue with throttling. Need clear SLOs to propose.
- Bring numbers: P95 increased from 220ms -> 410ms after PR #1128; token throughput unchanged. Add percentages and specific invocation examples.

Current state overview (talking points):
- Latency regression observed since deploy 2028-06-04 (deploy: runtime PR #1128). Regression most visible at seq_len>1024 and for models using KV-cache warm path.
- Customer impact: two internal customers reported transient errors + one support ticket from early adopter (customer: AtlasAI). Not yet widespread but trending.
- What we've tried: revert last compile optimization locally (gives ~30% improvement), increased batching threshold (marginal), disabled a new attention padding path (improved p95 for long sequences).
- Hypothesis: compiler kernel selection now favors a new fused-attention kernel that behaves poorly for sequences with heavy KV reuse; fallback path not triggering correctly.

Evidence to present quickly:
- P95 per model family (small table in head): base-model-a: 220 -> 360ms; longform-16k: 480 -> 890ms; replication on staging with vbench shows same pattern.
- Trace sample: stage-run-20280608-17: shows a single kernel call taking 280ms vs expected 40ms.
- Regression appears correlated with recent llvm-kernel bump (commit sha ab12f).

Proposed immediate options (clear asks for manager):
1) Rollback PR #1128 on staging/hosted for canary customers until we root cause. Pros: fast rollback isolating cause. Cons: reintroduces prior resource usage and potentially higher cost.
2) Short-term mitigation: add selective kernel fallback for seq_len>1024 and apply on production for ~10% of traffic. Pros: limited blast radius, keeps rollout mostly live. Cons: complexity + needs QA.
3) Continue with current rollout and prioritize a fix in the next sprint (risk: more customer impact).

What I need from manager in the meeting:
- Decision preference (rollback vs selective fallback). If rollback, support with comms template and sign-off path.
- Priority bump for an extra infra SRE half-day to help validate fallback config and run canary tests.
- Headcount ask: short-term contractor for kernel QA if we pursue option 2 (estimate 2–4 weeks).

Career / 1:1 check-in (quick):
- Pulse: feeling stretched but motivated; recent on-call was heavy (2 midnights).
- Wins to call out: led the deflake for model-loading on dedicated nodes; improved startup time by ~15% which fed into Dedicated latency metrics.
- Development ask: want pairing time with compiler team (Amit) to level up on kernel debugging. Can manager help unblock 2–3 pairing sessions next sprint?
- Promotion timeline: still aiming for senior eng review in Q4. Need clearer signal on scope expansion (mentorship, design ownership) — propose owning the outbound perf incident postmortem and the plan.

Blockers & operational needs:
- Test infra: need a synthetic traffic harness for long-seq KV-warm workload (ticket in INF-2384, currently low infra priority).
- Cross-team: need compiler team to replicate the kernel p95 locally (Amit volunteered but calendar conflicts).
- Docs: runbook needs update for kernel fallback configuration (I can draft but need review).

Follow-up actions (assignments to capture in meeting):
- Action 1: Manager to approve short SRE assist (half-day) and confirm SRE point (owner: Priya Nair) — due: 2028-06-14.
- Action 2: I will prepare rollback SOP + comms draft if we choose option 1 (owner: Harper) — due: 2028-06-13 EOD.
- Action 3: Schedule pairing sessions with compiler lead (owner: Harper + Amit) — target: 2 sessions before 2028-06-21.
- Action 4: Open contractor req for kernel QA (owner: Harper; manager to approve) — draft posted to hiring channel by 2028-06-15.
- Action 5: Quick canary run with selective fallback for 5% traffic (owner: Priya) — run window: 2028-06-14 09:00-11:00 PT. Capture telemetry and rollback plan.

Post-meeting reminders:
- Update INF-2384 with outcomes and link to canary run artifacts.
- If rollback decision: update runbook and notify CS with templated note (outline below).

CS comms template (scratch):
- Subject: Update on performance anomaly (hosted inference)
- Body: Hi {customer}, we observed a transient performance regression affecting long-context workloads starting 2028-06-04. We have identified the root cause candidate and are running a limited canary/rollback to restore expected performance. No data was compromised. We will follow up with a timeline and next steps within 24 hours.

Open questions I want to ask during the 1:1: 
- What level of risk tolerance do you want for canary traffic vs full rollback here?
- If we escalate to incident commander, can I count on you for quick approver turnaround for rollback?
- For my promotion signal: which project (ownership of postmortem vs kernel QA lead) would you prefer I take to show org-level impact?

Notes-to-self (post-meeting):
- Keep this doc short and convert to a Confluence incident timeline only if we do rollback.
- Save traces and p95 graphs into a single artifact (s3://redwood-dev/latency-traces/2028-06-08/).
- Follow-up with Amit right after the 1:1 to lock pairing slots.

Random scribbles / fragments for meeting if time:
- "If rollback, state: temporary rollback to PRE-1128 optimizer; will reintroduce earlier memory profile by ~8% but restores p95."
- "Canary plan: 5% traffic for 2 hours, ramp to 25% if stable, rollback on >20% regression from baseline."

End of scratchpad.
